articles.title: Pedestrian seriously injured after being struck by vehicle in Richmond Hill
articles.summary: A pedestrian was rushed to a hospital with serious injuries Thursday morning after being struck by a vehicle in Richmond Hill, according to police. articles.title: Several road closures expected downtown Toronto for ‘National Peace Officer Memorial Run’
articles.summary: Several roads in downtown Toronto will see rolling closures Thursday morning as hundreds of police officers take part in the annual National Peace Officer’s Memorial Run. articles.title: Netanyahu arrives in New York to address the UN, and other Mideast developments
articles.summary: Israel's increasingly isolated Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has arrived in New York to address the United Nations General Assembly, but no meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump is planned.

articles.title: Judge orders White House to restore access to CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Reporters still blocked
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — A federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump’s ban of three news outlets from the White House grounds, ordering early Thursday that CNN, MS NOW and Politico must have their access restored. Reporters for two of the outlets, however, were denied entry hours after the ruling.

articles.title: What Mark Carney’s new plan could mean for Pearson travellers
articles.summary: It’s been a week since Prime Minister Mark Carney said he wants private investors to take over operations at Canada's four largest airports, including Toronto's Pearson airport. And there are still questions around how it could affect travellers. CBC's Talia Ricci breaks down what we know.

articles.title: Police investigating fire at Leslieville store selling Hells Angels merchandise
articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating a fire that broke out Wednesday at a Leslieville retail store connected to the Hells Angels. They say the fire is now considered suspicious and they are still trying to determine the cause.
